chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would delay any missed fasting until the month of Sha'ban, out of reluctance to prevent the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from their needs. So when it became Sha'ban, they would fast, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would say, 'Sha'ban is my month.'

As for the narrations that came regarding the prohibition of fasting in Sha'ban and that no one among the Imams (peace be upon them) fasted it, the meaning is that no one among the Imams (peace be upon them) fasted it on the basis that its fasting runs the course of the month of Ramadan in terms of obligation and necessity, because a group said that fasting it is obligatory, and Abu al-Khattab (may Allah curse him) and his companions went to this view and said that whoever breaks a day of it incurs the same expiation as one who breaks a day of Ramadan. So the rejection of this came from them (peace be upon them), and that no one among them fasted it in this manner.

And the narrations that included the distinction between the month of Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan, the meaning is the prohibition of al-wisal (continuous fasting without breaking), which we explained previously as being prohibited.

And the news we previously cited from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), indicates this interpretation, when he said: I said to him, 'Does he not distinguish between them?' He said, 'If he breaks his fast at night, that is a distinction. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) only said, "There is no wisal in fasting."'
He means that the man does not fast two consecutive days without breaking his fast. And it is recommended for the man not to leave the suhur (pre-dawn meal).

key_terms.الْوِصَالُ: Wisal (continuous fasting for two or more days without eating)
key_terms.شَعْبَانُ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting in the month of Sha'ban and the meaning of Wisal?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s wives delaying their *qada* fasts in Sha'ban to avoid *wisal* (continuous fasting) and neglecting marital intimacy, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s declaration 'Sha'ban is my month.' Shia scholars clarify that prohibitions against fasting in Sha'ban often target the Isawiyyah sect’s view of its obligation or the specific act of *wisal*, rather than fasting in general, while also recommending the preservation of *suhur* as a key element of the fast.
